sentences.en: In 2011, the body of a woman was discovered in a California vineyard.
sentences.zh: 2011年，一名女性的遗体在加利福尼亚州的一个葡萄园中被发现。

sentences.en: She had been decapitated, and her body had been drained of blood.
sentences.zh: 她遭到斩首，体内血液已被放干。

sentences.en: It appeared her killer had gone to extraordinary lengths to conceal her identity.
sentences.zh: 凶手似乎费尽心机，试图掩盖她的身份。

sentences.en: For more than a decade, she was known only as Jane Doe.
sentences.zh: 十多年来，她一直被称为“无名氏”。

sentences.en: Then, detectives finally learned her name, Ada.
sentences.zh: 后来，侦探们终于查明了她的名字——艾达。

sentences.en: But, identifying her only made this bizarre murder even more perplexing.
sentences.zh: 然而，确认她的身份反而让这起离奇的谋杀案变得更加扑朔迷离。

sentences.en: Ada is the new series from Casefile Presents, available now wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 《艾达》是“Casefile Presents”推出的全新系列节目，现已在各大播客平台上线。

sentences.en: The Christian Bible is composed of 66 books, which are divided into the Old Testament, based primarily on the Hebrew Bible, and the New Testament,
sentences.zh: 基督教《圣经》由66卷书组成，分为主要基于希伯来《圣经》的《旧约》和

sentences.en: an exploration of the teachings and life of Jesus ChriSt.
sentences.zh: 探索耶稣基督生平与教义的《新约》。

sentences.en: The very final book of the Bible is the Book of Revelation, a 22-chapter series penned by a prophet known as John of Patmos.
sentences.zh: 《圣经》的最后一卷书是《启示录》，这是一部由先知拔摩岛的约翰所撰写的22章系列书。

sentences.en: It is an apocalyptic text that details a spiritual battle between good and evil, culminating in Jesus returning to earth.
sentences.zh: 这是一部启示录式的文本，详细描述了善与恶之间的属灵战争，最终以耶稣重返人间告终。

sentences.en: Combining warnings to followers with prophecies about the future, the Book of Revelation anticipates the ultimate defeat of Satan and a final judgment passed on all human beings.
sentences.zh: 《启示录》结合了对信徒的警示和对未来的预言，预示了撒旦的最终失败以及对全人类的终极审判。

sentences.en: Those deemed worthy by their deeds during life and their adherence to Christ will be saved, resurrected to live in a new heaven and earth free from pain, suffering and death.
sentences.zh: 那些因生前善行和对基督的忠诚而被视为配得的人将获得拯救，复活后生活在没有痛苦、苦难和死亡的新天新地中。

sentences.en: Unbelievers and individuals deemed to be wicked will be sentenced to a lake of fire, a final demise and the ultimate punishment for lost souls, dubbed the Second Death.
sentences.zh: 不信者和被视为邪恶的人将被判入火湖，这是迷失灵魂的最终结局和终极惩罚，被称为“第二次死亡”。

sentences.en: The mysterious language of the Book of Revelation and its many prophecies have led to countless Christian scholars, leaders and adherents
sentences.zh: 《启示录》中神秘的语言及其众多的预言，促使无数基督教学者、领袖和信徒

sentences.en: attempting to predict when this end of the world will come.
sentences.zh: 试图预测世界末日何时到来。

sentences.en: In chapter 5 of the book, John of Patmos introduces the prophecy of the Seven Seals, seven separate events that will take place between Jesus' lifetime
sentences.zh: 在《启示录》第5章中，拔摩岛的约翰引入了“七印”的预言，即在耶稣在世期间

sentences.en: and his eventual return, known as the Second Coming.
sentences.zh: 到他最终回归（即“第二次降临”）之间将发生的七个独立事件。

sentences.en: These prophecies are written on a book or a scroll sealed shut with seven wax seals, which no one but a figure dubbed the Lamb of God is able to open.
sentences.zh: 这些预言写在一卷用七个蜡封封住的书卷上，除了被称为“上帝的羔羊”的人物外，无人能将其打开。

sentences.en: Quote,
sentences.zh: 引用如下：

sentences.en: Then I saw in the right hand of him who sat on the throne a scroll with writing on both sides and sealed with seven seals.
sentences.zh: 我看见坐宝座的手中有书卷，里外都写着字，用七印封严了。

sentences.en: And I saw a mighty angel proclaiming in a loud voice,
sentences.zh: 我又看见一位大力的天使大声宣告：

sentences.en: Who is worthy to break the seals and open the scroll?
sentences.zh: 有谁配展开那书卷，揭开那七印呢？

sentences.en: But no one in heaven or on earth or under the earth could open the scroll or even look inside it.
sentences.zh: 只是在天上、地上、地底下，没有能展开、能观看那书卷的。

sentences.en: I wept and wept because no one was found who was worthy to open the scroll or look inside.
sentences.zh: 因为没有配展开、配观看那书卷的，我就大哭。

sentences.en: Then one of the elders said to me,
sentences.zh: 长老中有一位对我说：

sentences.en: Do not weep.
sentences.zh: 不要哭。

sentences.en: See, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has triumphed.
sentences.zh: 看哪，犹大支派中的狮子，大卫的根，他已得胜。

sentences.en: He is able to open the scroll and its seven seals.
sentences.zh: 他能以展开那书卷，揭开那七印。

sentences.en: Then I saw a lamb, looking as if it had been slain, standing at the centre of the throne, encircled by the four living creatures and the elders.
sentences.zh: 我又看见宝座与四活物，并长老之中，有羔羊站立，像是被杀过的。

sentences.en: The lamb had seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven spirits of God sent out into all the earth.
sentences.zh: 羔羊有七角七眼，就是神的七灵，奉差遣往普天下去的。

sentences.en: He went and took the scroll from the right hand of him who sat on the throne.
sentences.zh: 这羔羊前来，从坐宝座的右手中拿了书卷。

sentences.en: Traditionally, the Lamb of God has been interpreted as Jesus himself, whom Christians believe was sacrificed to atone for humanity's sins.
sentences.zh: 传统上，“上帝的羔羊”被解释为耶稣本人，基督徒相信他为赎世人的罪而牺牲。

sentences.en: Just as actual lambs were sacrificed in stories of the Old Testament.
sentences.zh: 正如《旧约》故事中真正的羔羊被献祭一样。

sentences.en: However, some individuals have used scripture to argue that this lamb was a different messiah who would assist Jesus in the final spiritual battle.
sentences.zh: 然而，有些人利用经文辩称，这只羔羊是另一位弥赛亚，他将协助耶稣进行最后的属灵战争。

sentences.en: They found more passages in other parts of the Bible that also prophesied a second messiah, whose name was Cyrus the Great.
sentences.zh: 他们在《圣经》的其他部分发现了更多预言第二位弥赛亚的段落，其名为居鲁士大帝。

sentences.en: In Hebrew, the name Cyrus translates to Koresh.
sentences.zh: 在希伯来语中，居鲁士的名字译为“科雷什”。

sentences.en: The Seventh-day Adventist church originated in the state of New York during the 1840s and places a particular emphasis on the impending second coming of ChriSt.
sentences.zh: 基督复临安息日会于19世纪40年代起源于纽约州，特别强调基督即将第二次降临。

sentences.en: The name Adventist stems from the group's belief that Jesus will soon return to earth,
sentences.zh: “复临”一词源于该组织相信耶稣即将重返地球，

sentences.en: with several pioneers of the Adventist faith attempting to predict when his return would occur.
sentences.zh: 几位复临信仰的先驱曾试图预测他回归的时间。

sentences.en: Although opinions have differed, a consistent theme is that Christ will return after a period of turmoil.
sentences.zh: 尽管观点各异，但一个核心主题是：基督将在经历一段动荡时期后回归。

sentences.en: In addition to this emphasis on the second coming,
sentences.zh: 除了对第二次降临的强调外，

sentences.en: Seventh-day Adventism has a number of other defining features.
sentences.zh: 基督复临安息日会还有许多其他显著特征。

sentences.en: Bible study must be ongoing and is crucial to the faith, as all truth that can be known lies within its passages.
sentences.zh: 《圣经》学习必须持续进行，这对信仰至关重要，因为所有可知的真理都蕴含在经文之中。

sentences.en: By the early 1920s, the Seventh-day Adventist church had spread from the east coast of America to the west, as well as overseas.
sentences.zh: 到20世纪20年代初，基督复临安息日会已从美国东海岸扩展到西海岸，并传播至海外。

sentences.en: One adherent to the faith was an immigrant from Bulgaria named Victor Hotef.
sentences.zh: 该信仰的一位信徒是来自保加利亚的移民，名叫维克多·霍特夫。

sentences.en: Victor had immigrated to the US at the age of 22 and initially lived in Illinois, before later relocating to California.
sentences.zh: 维克多22岁时移民美国，最初住在伊利诺伊州，后来搬到了加利福尼亚州。

sentences.en: Although he was originally baptised in the Bulgarian Orthodox Church,
sentences.zh: 虽然他最初是在保加利亚正教会受洗的，

sentences.en: Victor later converted to Seventh-day Adventism in 1919 at the age of 34.
sentences.zh: 但维克多后来在1919年、34岁时改信了基督复临安息日会。

sentences.en: He became consumed by his faith and spent all of his spare time when he wasn't working, pouring over the Bible, especially the Book of Revelation.
sentences.zh: 他全身心投入信仰，工作之余的所有时间都用来研读《圣经》，尤其是《启示录》。

sentences.en: While earning a living as a washing machine repairman,
sentences.zh: 在以修理洗衣机为生的同时，

sentences.en: Victor also taught classes at a Seventh-day Adventist Sabbath school, a weekly religious education program held on Saturday mornings before church service.
sentences.zh: 维克多还在基督复临安息日会的安息日学校教课，这是一个每周六上午在礼拜前举行的宗教教育项目。

sentences.en: Victor began to worry that other members of his faith weren't taking it seriously enough.
sentences.zh: 维克多开始担心该信仰的其他成员不够认真对待教义。

sentences.en: He made a list of problems he had observed in other congregants, including a disbelief in prophecy, selling church merchandise, following earthly trends and fashions too closely,
sentences.zh: 他列出了一份在其他信徒身上观察到的问题清单，包括不相信预言、兜售教会商品、盲目追随世俗潮流和时尚，

sentences.en: and a lack of reverence.
sentences.zh: 以及缺乏敬畏之心。

sentences.en: When Victor began speaking more openly about his concerns in his classes and at other Adventist gatherings, church elders took note and asked him to stop.
sentences.zh: 当维克多开始在课堂和其他复临信徒聚会上更公开地谈论他的担忧时，教会长老注意到了这一点，并要求他停止。

sentences.en: They also objected to some of his interpretations of scripture.
sentences.zh: 他们还反对他的一些经文解读。

sentences.en: Victor refused, and in 1930 he published a manuscript titled
sentences.zh: 维克多拒绝了，并于1930年出版了一份手稿，题为

sentences.en: The Shepherd's Rod, in which he called for denominational reform and a recommitment from all Seventh-day Adventists.
sentences.zh: 《牧羊人的杖》，他在书中呼吁进行教派改革，并要求所有基督复临安息日会信徒重新委身。

sentences.en: Victor predicted that the second coming of Christ was imminent and that soon there would be an apocalypse where Christ's warriors would defeat the evil armies of Babylon,
sentences.zh: 维克多预言基督的第二次降临迫在眉睫，很快就会发生一场启示录式的战争，基督的战士将击败巴比伦的邪恶军队，

sentences.en: a term Seventh-day Adventists used to refer to the fallen state of traditional Christianity.
sentences.zh: 这是基督复临安息日会用来指代传统基督教堕落状态的一个术语。

sentences.en: That same year, Victor's actions led to him being disfellowshipped by the church, but he maintained a strong following of his own.
sentences.zh: 同年，维克多的行为导致他被教会开除，但他仍拥有一批坚定的追随者。

sentences.en: When he could no longer teach Sabbath school in church, he continued to do so at a house across the road.
sentences.zh: 当他无法再在教会教授安息日学校课程时，他便转而在马路对面的一所房子里继续授课。

sentences.en: Some study groups at different Adventist churches across the country worked off his ideas, which led to those who promoted Victor's material being disfellowshipped too.
sentences.zh: 全国各地不同复临教会的一些学习小组开始研究他的思想，这导致那些推广维克多资料的人也被开除。

sentences.en: Eventually, the church declared Victor's work to be outright heresy and in 1934 he began his own organisation called The Shepherd's Rod.
sentences.zh: 最终，教会宣布维克多的著作是彻头彻尾的异端，1934年，他成立了自己的组织，名为“牧羊人的杖”。

sentences.en: This was later officially renamed The Davidian Seventh-day Adventists.
sentences.zh: 后来该组织正式更名为“大卫支派基督复临安息日会”。

sentences.en: The name Davidian stemmed from Victor Hotef's belief that he was destined to restore the Davidic Kingdom, the historic Kingdom of Israel ruled over by descendants of King David.
sentences.zh: “大卫支派”这一名称源于维克多·霍特夫的信念，即他注定要恢复大卫王国，即由大卫王后裔统治的以色列历史王国。

sentences.en: A direct ancestor of Jesus, King David's lineage is key to Christianity's messianic prophecies.
sentences.zh: 作为耶稣的直系祖先，大卫王的血统是基督教弥赛亚预言的关键。

sentences.en: Seeking a base that would allow him to establish headquarters for his new church,
sentences.zh: 为了寻找一个可以建立新教会总部的基地，

sentences.en: Victor scoured a map of the United States looking for a suitable place.
sentences.zh: 维克多仔细查看了美国地图，寻找合适的地方。

sentences.en: He wanted somewhere with cheap land and a culture receptive to religion.
sentences.zh: 他想要一个土地便宜且文化上容易接受宗教的地方。

sentences.en: By 1935, he'd found a location that fit perfectly and purchased almost 200 acres of land that sat northwest of the Texan city of Waco.
sentences.zh: 到1935年，他找到了一个完美的地方，并购买了位于德克萨斯州韦科市西北部近200英亩的土地。

sentences.en: Sitting deep in the heartland of Texas, wedged some distance between the progressive capital of Austin and major city Dallas,
sentences.zh: 这里深处德克萨斯州腹地，夹在进步的州首府奥斯汀和主要城市达拉斯之间，

sentences.en: Waco was then a small conservative city primarily known for being the birthplace of the soft drink,
sentences.zh: 当时的韦科是一个保守的小城市，主要以软饮料“胡椒博士”的诞生地而闻名，

sentences.en: Dr. Pepper.
sentences.zh: 即Dr. Pepper。

sentences.en: Other than that, there was little that stood out about it.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，它并没有什么特别之处。

sentences.en: In 1935, its population sat at around 55,000.
Located on the banks of the Brazos River and built in a valley-like area,
sentences.zh: 韦科坐落在布拉索斯河畔，建在一个类似山谷的地区，

sentences.en: Waco was also home to Baylor University, a private Baptist college where students were expected to abstain from alcohol, premarital sex, and dancing.
sentences.zh: 也是贝勒大学的所在地，这是一所私立浸信会学院，学生被要求戒酒、禁绝婚前性行为和跳舞。

sentences.en: Even within the religious state of Texas,
sentences.zh: 即使在宗教氛围浓厚的德克萨斯州，

sentences.en: Waco had a fervour that was seen as particularly strong.
sentences.zh: 韦科的宗教狂热也被认为特别强烈。

sentences.en: According to author Jeff Gwynn, other Texans nicknamed the city Jerusalem on the Brazos and the buckle of the Bible Belt.
sentences.zh: 据作家杰夫·格温称，其他德克萨斯人给这座城市起了个绰号，叫“布拉索斯河上的耶路撒冷”和“圣经带的扣环”。

sentences.en: These were unofficial titles that Waco residents took pride in.
sentences.zh: 这些是非官方的头衔，韦科居民对此引以为豪。

sentences.en: The land purchased by Victor Hotef was seven miles northwest of the city limits and lay on the shores of Lake Waco.
sentences.zh: 维克多·霍特夫购买的土地位于市界西北七英里处，坐落在韦科湖岸边。

sentences.en: Victor named his headquarters Mount Carmel in honour of a biblical passage found in the book of Micah
sentences.zh: 维克多将他的总部命名为“迦密山”，以纪念《弥迦书》中的一段经文，

sentences.en: that describes the land of Judah becoming desolate due to people's wicked deeds.
sentences.zh: 该经文描述了犹大地因人们的邪恶行为而变得荒凉。

sentences.en: God is then asked to shepherd his people who are living in the midst of Carmel.
sentences.zh: 随后，人们祈求上帝牧养居住在迦密山中的子民。

sentences.en: The passage is one of hope for a miraculous rescue and a peaceful, bountiful future.
sentences.zh: 这段经文寄托了对奇迹般拯救以及和平、富饶未来的希望。

sentences.en: Roughly 120 people moved to Mount Carmel with Victor Hotef and they built a community there.
sentences.zh: 大约120人随维克多·霍特夫搬到了迦密山，并在那里建立了一个社区。

sentences.en: In addition to working on the property and for surrounding neighbourhoods, the Davidians still worked to bring more converts to their church.
sentences.zh: 除了在地产上工作和为周边社区服务外，大卫支派信徒仍致力于为教会争取更多信徒。

sentences.en: They acquired a printing press and used it to publish Victor's sermons, which were then sent to every Seventh-day Adventist whose address was available.
sentences.zh: 他们购置了一台印刷机，用来出版维克多的布道词，然后寄给每一位地址可查的基督复临安息日会信徒。

sentences.en: Victor did not claim to be a messianic figure, but his followers saw him as a prophet who could foretell the coming of a new saviour.
sentences.zh: 维克多并未声称自己是弥赛亚，但他的追随者视他为能预言新救世主降临的先知。

sentences.en: As the years passed, Mount Carmel grew both in size and population.
sentences.zh: 随着岁月流逝，迦密山的规模和人口不断增长。

sentences.en: In 1937, the now 52-year-old Victor Hotef married Florence Hermanson, the 17-year-old daughter of two of his most devoted followers.
sentences.zh: 1937年，时年52岁的维克多·霍特夫娶了17岁的弗洛伦斯·赫曼森，她是维克多最忠诚的两名追随者的女儿。

sentences.en: Some church members were disturbed by this significant age gap.
sentences.zh: 一些教会成员对如此巨大的年龄差距感到不安。

sentences.en: Florence became Victor's primary assistant, transcribing all of his sermons and assisting her husband in his ministry.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伦斯成为了维克多的主要助手，负责记录他所有的布道词，并协助丈夫进行传教工作。

sentences.en: Almost 20 years after Victor established Mount Carmel, he fell ill towards the end of 1954.
sentences.zh: 在维克多建立迦密山近20年后，他于1954年底病倒了。

sentences.en: He died of heart failure in February 1955, just a few weeks before his 70th birthday.
sentences.zh: 1955年2月，就在他70岁生日前几周，他因心脏衰竭去世。

sentences.en: Shocked and shaken by the sudden loss of their leader, the Davidians' future seemed uncertain.
sentences.zh: 领袖突然离世，大卫支派信徒感到震惊和动摇，未来似乎变得不确定。

sentences.en: But to their surprise, Victor's widow Florence Hotef explained they didn't need to wonder about the path forward.
sentences.zh: 但令他们惊讶的是，维克多的遗孀弗洛伦斯·霍特夫解释说，他们不必为未来的道路感到迷茫。

sentences.en: As Victor lay dying in hospital, he'd revealed to Florence that he knew when the end time would arrive, four years from now, on Wednesday, April 22, 1959.
sentences.zh: 维克多在医院弥留之际曾向弗洛伦斯透露，他知道末日何时到来：四年后的1959年4月22日，星期三。

sentences.en: Jesus would arrive on Earth along with a holy, cleansing fire, and only 144,000 people known as the elect would survive this apocalypse.
sentences.zh: 届时，耶稣将带着神圣的净化之火降临地球，只有144,000名被称为“选民”的人才能在这次启示录中幸存。

sentences.en: After it was over, they would emerge triumphant and live happily in God's new kingdom on Earth.
sentences.zh: 灾难过后，他们将凯旋，并在上帝的新王国中幸福地生活在地球上。

sentences.en: Florence explained that Victor had tasked her with taking over the church's leadership and recruiting many more members in anticipation of the imminent spiritual battle.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伦斯解释说，维克多已委任她接管教会领导权，并为迎接即将到来的属灵战争招募更多成员。

sentences.en: Not everyone agreed with Florence leading the Davidians.
sentences.zh: 并非所有人都同意由弗洛伦斯领导大卫支派。

sentences.en: One member named Benjamin Roden claimed that he'd received messages from God that he should be the new leader.
sentences.zh: 一名叫本杰明·罗登的成员声称，他收到了上帝的启示，他才是新的领袖。

sentences.en: But Florence Hotef and the church's executive council refuted this.
sentences.zh: 但弗洛伦斯·霍特夫和教会执行委员会驳回了这一说法。

sentences.en: Over the next few years, the Davidians worked at recruiting more members.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几年里，大卫支派信徒致力于招募更多成员。

sentences.en: They purchased more land east of Waco, a sprawling 941 acres in a rather desolate scrubland area with the address 1781 Double E Ranch Road.
sentences.zh: 他们在韦科以东购买了更多土地，这是一片荒凉的灌木丛地区，占地941英亩，地址为双E牧场路1781号。

sentences.en: This land was dubbed New Mount Carmel, and members used cheap materials to build a church, a main building, and some shacks that would serve as residences.
sentences.zh: 这片土地被称为“新迦密山”，成员们用廉价材料建造了一座教堂、一栋主楼和一些用作住所的棚屋。

sentences.en: Tents, trucks, and buses were also used as additional accommodation.
sentences.zh: 帐篷、卡车和公共汽车也被用作额外的住宿设施。

sentences.en: The Davidians also began broadcasting recruitment messages, purchasing a weekly time slot on ABC Radio.
sentences.zh: 大卫支派信徒还开始广播招募信息，购买了ABC电台的每周时段。

sentences.en: Their show was called The Eleventh Hour Call and was recorded from a studio they'd built at New Mount Carmel.
sentences.zh: 他们的节目名为《第十一小时的呼唤》，是在他们于新迦密山建造的工作室录制的。

sentences.en: As Wednesday, April 22, 1959 neared, the group sold their personal possessions, gave their money to the church, and sent out broadcasts and pamphlets encouraging people
sentences.zh: 随着1959年4月22日星期三的临近，该组织成员变卖了个人财产，将钱捐给教会，并发出广播和传单，鼓励人们

sentences.en: to join them at New Mount Carmel to await the impending end time.
sentences.zh: 加入他们，在新迦密山等待即将到来的末日。

sentences.en: Roughly 1,000 people heeded their call, descending on New Mount Carmel and crowding inside and around its chapel as they waited for the apocalypse to begin.
sentences.zh: 大约1,000人响应了他们的号召，涌向新迦密山，挤在礼拜堂内外，等待启示录的开始。

sentences.en: They waited all through Wednesday, April 22, with nothing happening.
sentences.zh: 他们整整等了一天，直到4月22日星期三结束，什么也没发生。

sentences.en: As midnight struck and the date ticked over to Thursday, April 23, most of the crowd left in New Mount Carmel en masse in a state of utter disillusionment.
sentences.zh: 午夜钟声敲响，日期转为4月23日星期四，留在新迦密山的绝大多数人群陷入了极度的幻灭，纷纷离去。

sentences.en: Newcomers who'd hoped to see Jesus return to Earth weren't the only ones disappointed.
sentences.zh: 那些希望看到耶稣重返地球的新来者并不是唯一感到失望的人。

sentences.en: Davidian members were left stunned by the failed prophecy.
sentences.zh: 大卫支派的成员们也被这次失败的预言惊呆了。

sentences.en: It even prompted some to doubt the legitimacy of their deceased founder, Victor Hotef.
sentences.zh: 这甚至促使一些人开始怀疑他们已故创始人维克多·霍特夫的合法性。

sentences.en: If he had indeed made the incorrect prediction that Florence had relayed, then he was no true prophet.
sentences.zh: 如果他确实做出了弗洛伦斯所传达的错误预测，那么他就不是真正的先知。

sentences.en: Some Davidians left Mount Carmel and returned to Seventh-day Adventism.
sentences.zh: 一些大卫支派信徒离开了迦密山，回到了基督复临安息日会。

sentences.en: Others abandoned their faith altogether.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则完全放弃了信仰。

sentences.en: In the wake of the failed end time, only about 50 Davidians remained.
sentences.zh: 在末日预言失败后，只剩下约50名大卫支派信徒。

sentences.en: Florence Hotef was not one of them.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伦斯·霍特夫并不在其中。

sentences.en: After informing her followers that she had been mistaken, she sold most of New Mount Carmel's land, relocated to California, and began working for tech giant IBM.
sentences.zh: 在告知追随者自己犯了错之后，她卖掉了新迦密山的大部分土地，搬到了加利福尼亚州，并开始为科技巨头IBM工作。

sentences.en: She later remarried and eventually passed away in 2008 at the age of 89.
sentences.zh: 她后来再婚，并于2008年去世，享年89岁。

sentences.en: With Florence out of the picture, another Davidian was ready to fill her shoes.
sentences.zh: 随着弗洛伦斯的离开，另一位大卫支派信徒准备接替她的位置。

sentences.en: Benjamin Roden had always objected to Florence succeeding her husband after his death and had long said that God wanted him to lead instead.
sentences.zh: 本杰明·罗登一直反对弗洛伦斯在丈夫死后继任，并长期声称上帝希望由他来领导。

sentences.en: Born into a Jewish family,
sentences.zh: 他出生于一个犹太家庭，

sentences.en: Benjamin had converted to Christianity and then Seventh-day Adventism after meeting his wife.
sentences.zh: 在遇见妻子后，本杰明改信了基督教，随后又加入了基督复临安息日会。

sentences.en: The couple had heard of Victor Hotef during the mid-1940s and relocated to Waco to join his church.
sentences.zh: 这对夫妇在20世纪40年代中期听说了维克多·霍特夫，并搬到韦科加入了他的教会。

sentences.en: Their admiration of Victor did not extend to his wife and Benjamin Roden had loudly disputed her claims that the end time would commence on April 22, 1959.
sentences.zh: 他们对维克多的钦佩并没有延伸到他的妻子身上，本杰明·罗登曾大声反驳她关于末日将于1959年4月22日开始的说法。

sentences.en: No one took much notice of his arguments until Florence's prophecy failed.
sentences.zh: 直到弗洛伦斯的预言失败，才有人注意到他的论点。

sentences.en: Under Benjamin's leadership, the Davidians became known as the Branch Davidians, with Benjamin adopting the term Branch from Biblical Scripture.
sentences.zh: 在本杰明的领导下，大卫支派信徒被称为“大卫支派分支”，本杰明采用了《圣经》中的“分支”一词。

sentences.en: In one passage he cited as an inspiration,
sentences.zh: 在他引用的一个灵感段落中，

sentences.en: Jesus told his followers,
sentences.zh: 耶稣告诉他的追随者：

sentences.en: I am the true vine, and you are the branches.
sentences.zh: 我是真葡萄树，你们是枝子。

sentences.en: Benjamin declared that the Christian holidays of Christmas and Easter were actually pagan celebrations with origins in the winter solstice and spring equinox.
sentences.zh: 本杰明宣称，圣诞节和复活节等基督教节日实际上是起源于冬至和春分的异教庆典。

sentences.en: From now on,
sentences.zh: 从现在起，

sentences.en: Branch Davidians would observe
sentences.zh: 大卫支派分支成员将遵守

sentences.en: Hebraic customs instead, celebrating the Jewish holidays of Passover,
sentences.zh: 希伯来习俗，庆祝逾越节、

sentences.en: Sukkot, and Old Testament feast days.
sentences.zh: 住棚节和《旧约》中的节期。

sentences.en: Benjamin purchased the 77 acres that remained of New Mount Carmel and was joined by about 40 followers.
sentences.zh: 本杰明购买了新迦密山剩余的77英亩土地，约有40名追随者加入了他的行列。

sentences.en: Although most of the Branch Davidians lived side by side at New Mount Carmel, they were by no means cut off from the broader community.
sentences.zh: 尽管大多数大卫支派分支成员在新迦密山共同生活，但他们绝没有与更广泛的社区隔绝。

sentences.en: Some of the children attended local public schools, while a number of adult members held jobs in downtown Waco.
sentences.zh: 一些孩子在当地公立学校上学，而许多成年成员则在韦科市中心工作。

sentences.en: A few worked as cashiers at various stores, others worked in manual labour as tradespeople and landscapers.
sentences.zh: 一些人担任商店收银员，另一些人则从事体力劳动，如技工和园艺师。

sentences.en: Benjamin's wife,
sentences.zh: 本杰明的妻子，

sentences.en: Lois Roden, was his second-in-command and biggest supporter.
sentences.zh: 洛伊丝·罗登，是他的副手和最大的支持者。

sentences.en: The couple acquired property in Israel with the intention of eventually moving their entire congregation to Jerusalem.
sentences.zh: 这对夫妇在以色列购置了房产，打算最终将整个会众迁往耶路撒冷。

sentences.en: Over the next two decades,
sentences.zh: 在接下来的二十年里，

sentences.en: Ben and Lois worked side by side with additional support from their eldest son, George.
sentences.zh: 本和洛伊丝并肩工作，并得到了他们长子乔治的额外支持。

sentences.en: George Roden was a big personality and he had a passion for building the church that some congregants found inspiring.
sentences.zh: 乔治·罗登个性鲜明，他对建设教会充满热情，这让一些信徒深受鼓舞。

sentences.en: But he could also be arrogant, with no interest in anyone's opinion but his own, and could also be both verbally and physically aggressive.
sentences.zh: 但他也很傲慢，除了自己的意见外，对任何人的看法都不屑一顾，而且在言语和肢体上都具有攻击性。

sentences.en: George's parents didn't like his attitude, but they appreciated his enthusiasm.
sentences.zh: 乔治的父母不喜欢他的态度，但他们欣赏他的热情。

sentences.en: Benjamin Roden, now aged in his mid-70s, fell sick, and his wife Lois took on a greater role in the church's leadership.
sentences.zh: 本杰明·罗登当时已年过七旬，身患重病，他的妻子洛伊丝在教会领导层中承担了更大的责任。

sentences.en: Lois, who was more than a decade younger than her husband, intended to take on the role of church president after Benjamin passed away.
sentences.zh: 洛伊丝比丈夫小十多岁，她打算在本杰明去世后接任教会主席一职。

sentences.en: At around this same time, she summoned a meeting of church members to share something amazing that had happened to her.
sentences.zh: 大约在同一时间，她召集了教会成员开会，分享了一件发生在她身上的神奇之事。

sentences.en: She had been awake at 2am reading a verse in the book of Revelation that referred to an angel descending from heaven when she looked outside her window
sentences.zh: 凌晨两点，她醒着阅读《启示录》中关于天使从天而降的经文时，看向窗外，

sentences.en: and saw a shining silver angel fly by.
sentences.zh: 看到一位闪耀的银色天使飞过。

sentences.en: Although the angel said nothing,
sentences.zh: 尽管天使什么也没说，

sentences.en: Lois intuitively knew that the angel was the embodiment of what she called the Holy Spirit Mother.
sentences.zh: 洛伊丝直觉地知道，这位天使就是她所称的“圣灵母亲”的化身。

sentences.en: In Christianity, a central doctrine is that of the Holy Trinity, the notion that God is one being existing as three co-equal persons, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
sentences.zh: 在基督教中，一个核心教义是“三位一体”，即上帝是一个存在，表现为三个同等的位格：圣父、圣子和圣灵。

sentences.en: The Father is God, the creator of the universe.
sentences.zh: 圣父是上帝，是宇宙的创造者。

sentences.en: The Son is Jesus Christ who came to earth in human form.
sentences.zh: 圣子是耶稣基督，以人的形式来到人间。

sentences.en: The Holy Spirit is the non-physical presence of God in daily life.
sentences.zh: 圣灵是上帝在日常生活中非物质的存在。

sentences.en: Lois explained that she had always believed the Holy Spirit was masculine in nature.
sentences.zh: 洛伊丝解释说，她一直认为圣灵本质上是阳性的。

sentences.en: Upon seeing the angel, she'd had a revelation that it was actually feminine.
sentences.zh: 但在看到那位天使后，她得到启示，圣灵实际上是阴性的。

sentences.en: The Holy Trinity blended both masculine and feminine energy.
sentences.zh: 三位一体融合了阳性和阴性的能量。

sentences.en: Some Branch Davidians reacted negatively to this message, believing it to be blasphemous.
sentences.zh: 一些大卫教派的分支成员对这一信息反应消极，认为这是亵渎神明。

sentences.en: But others were intrigued and receptive to the idea.
sentences.zh: 但其他人则对此感到好奇并乐于接受。

sentences.en: Benjamin Roden, who by this point was very sick, supported his wife and her vision was said to be evidence that she was a true prophet.
sentences.zh: 当时已病入膏肓的本杰明·罗登支持他的妻子，并称她的异象证明了她是一位真正的先知。

sentences.en: When Benjamin died on October 22, 1978,
sentences.zh: 1978年10月22日，本杰明去世，

sentences.en: Lois became the new
sentences.zh: 洛伊丝成为了

sentences.en: Branch Davidian president.
sentences.zh: 大卫教派分支的新任主席。

sentences.en: Her son George was not happy about this.
sentences.zh: 她的儿子乔治对此很不高兴。

sentences.en: George was an ambitious person who believed he was destined to lead.
sentences.zh: 乔治是一个野心勃勃的人，他认为自己注定要成为领导者。

sentences.en: Several years earlier, in 1976, the then 38-year-old George ran in the United States presidential election, nominating himself as a Democratic candidate.
sentences.zh: 几年前的1976年，当时38岁的乔治曾参加美国总统大选，提名自己为民主党候选人。

sentences.en: According to author Jeff Gwynn, there is no evidence that he received a single vote in either the Democratic primary or the national election.
sentences.zh: 据作家杰夫·格温称，没有证据表明他在民主党初选或全国大选中获得过哪怕一张选票。

sentences.en: He now turned his attention to taking on his father's role as church leader, as he'd long seen himself as the natural heir.
sentences.zh: 现在，他将注意力转向接替父亲的教会领袖职位，因为他一直视自己为理所当然的继承人。

sentences.en: George called for a leadership election.
sentences.zh: 乔治要求进行领导权选举。

sentences.en: His mother won in a landslide.
sentences.zh: 他的母亲以压倒性优势获胜。

sentences.en: Undeterred,
sentences.zh: 乔治并未气馁，

sentences.en: George continued to badger the Branch Davidians and declare himself the rightful leader.
sentences.zh: 他继续纠缠大卫教派的成员，并宣称自己才是合法的领导者。

sentences.en: This prompted Lois to obtain a restraining order against her son, barring him from New Mount Carmel.
sentences.zh: 这促使洛伊丝对儿子申请了限制令，禁止他进入新迦密山。

sentences.en: George left and split his time between Texas and California.
sentences.zh: 乔治离开了，往返于德克萨斯州和加利福尼亚州之间。

sentences.en: But sometimes he defied the court order and returned to New Mount Carmel, lurking around its perimeters.
sentences.zh: 但有时他会无视法院禁令，回到新迦密山，在周边徘徊。

sentences.en: He refused to give up his ambition of leading the Branch Davidians and would argue his case both in person and in long, rambling letters.
sentences.zh: 他拒绝放弃领导大卫教派分支的野心，并会亲自或通过冗长杂乱的信件为自己辩解。

sentences.en: Lois continued running the church as well as travelling both domestically and overseas to proselytise.
sentences.zh: 洛伊丝继续管理教会，并奔波于国内外进行传教。

sentences.en: By the early 1980s,
sentences.zh: 到了20世纪80年代初，

sentences.en: Lois was in her mid-60s and mindful that she needed to come up with a succession plan.
sentences.zh: 洛伊丝已年过六旬，她意识到自己需要制定一个继任计划。

sentences.en: George showed no signs of giving up his goal of taking over the Branch Davidians, which was not what Lois wanted.
sentences.zh: 乔治毫无放弃接管大卫教派分支目标的迹象，这并非洛伊丝所愿。

sentences.en: She needed to find someone else to be the church's next prophet.
sentences.zh: 她需要找到其他人来担任教会的下一任先知。

sentences.zh: Casefile节目稍后回来。

sentences.zh: 通过支持我们的赞助商，您也在支持Casefile继续提供优质内容。

sentences.en: One day during the summer of 1981, two young friends drove down to Waco from the east Texas city of Tyler after hearing reports that there was a woman at New Mount Carmel
sentences.zh: 1981年夏天的某一天，两位年轻的朋友从德克萨斯州东部的泰勒市开车前往韦科，因为他们听说新迦密山有一位女性

sentences.en: who was a true prophet.
sentences.zh: 是真正的先知。

sentences.en: The journey took over two hours for 21-year-old
sentences.zh: 对于21岁的

sentences.en: Vernon Howell and his friend Harriet, whom he'd met at a Seventh-day
sentences.zh: 弗农·豪威尔和他的朋友哈丽特来说，这段旅程花了两个多小时，他们是在家乡的基督复临安息日会

sentences.en: Adventist church back home.
sentences.zh: 教堂认识的。

sentences.en: Vernon had already experienced a lot of instability in his young life.
sentences.zh: 弗农在年轻时就已经历了许多动荡。

sentences.en: His mother had given birth to him when she was just 14 years old and his father, six years her senior, had been a distant presence, refusing to even visit Vernon when he was born.
sentences.zh: 他母亲生他时年仅14岁，而比她大六岁的父亲一直很疏远，甚至在弗农出生时都不愿去探望。

sentences.en: Vernon and his mother
sentences.zh: 弗农和他的母亲

sentences.en: Bonnie lived with various extended family members until Bonnie married when Vernon was two years old.
sentences.zh: 邦妮曾与多位亲戚住在一起，直到弗农两岁时邦妮结婚。

sentences.en: Her new husband spanked Vernon as punishment in a way
sentences.zh: 她的新丈夫以一种

sentences.en: Bonnie felt was excessive.
sentences.zh: 邦妮认为过分的方式惩罚弗农，对他进行鞭打。

sentences.en: She left her husband but felt overwhelmed by her situation as a young single mother in a conservative and judgmental community.
sentences.zh: 她离开了丈夫，但作为一个生活在保守且爱评头论足的社区里的年轻单身母亲，她感到不堪重负。

sentences.en: She gave Vernon to her mother to raise, believing this was in his best interests.
sentences.zh: 她把弗农交给自己的母亲抚养，认为这对他是最好的。

sentences.en: Vernon's grandmother posed as his mother.
sentences.zh: 弗农的祖母冒充了他的母亲。

sentences.en: When Bonnie visited him, she pretended to be his aunt.
sentences.zh: 当邦妮来看望他时，她假装是他的阿姨。

sentences.en: By the time
sentences.zh: 到了

sentences.en: Vernon was five,
sentences.zh: 弗农五岁时，

sentences.en: Bonnie had remarried a merchant marine named Roy and felt well enough to care for her son again.
sentences.zh: 邦妮改嫁给了一位名叫罗伊的商船海员，并觉得有能力再次照顾儿子了。

sentences.en: When she told
sentences.zh: 当她告诉

sentences.en: Vernon who she really was to him, the truth left him feeling shocked, confused, and as though his entire world had just tipped upside down.
sentences.zh: 弗农她与他的真实关系时，真相让他感到震惊、困惑，仿佛整个世界都颠倒了。

sentences.en: He moved in with Bonnie and Roy, who was a disciplinarian and difficult for Vernon to get along with.
sentences.zh: 他搬去和邦妮及罗伊一起住，罗伊是个严厉的人，弗农很难与他相处。

sentences.en: His parents soon had another child named Roger who appeared to Vernon to be the favourite.
sentences.zh: 他的父母不久又生了一个孩子叫罗杰，在弗农看来，罗杰似乎更受宠爱。

sentences.en: Vernon would later say,
sentences.zh: 弗农后来曾说：

sentences.en: I was always getting whooped by Roy for everything while Roger got away with murder.
sentences.zh: “我总是因为各种琐事被罗伊毒打，而罗杰却能逃脱惩罚。”

sentences.en: Vernon would also later reveal that at around the same time that he reunited with his mother, one of his male relatives began sexually abusing him.
sentences.zh: 弗农后来还透露，大约在他与母亲重聚的同一时期，他的一位男性亲属开始对他进行性虐待。

sentences.en: The abuse, which included rape, went on for four years.
sentences.zh: 这种虐待包括强奸，持续了四年之久。

sentences.en: He never revealed the identity of his abuser as he didn't want to upset his mother.
sentences.zh: 他从未透露施虐者的身份，因为他不想让母亲难过。

sentences.en: Vernon struggled at school due to a learning disorder that has been speculated to have been attention deficit hyperactive disorder or ADHD.
sentences.zh: 弗农在学校表现挣扎，因为他患有学习障碍，据推测可能是注意力缺陷多动障碍（ADHD）。

sentences.en: But he loved church.
sentences.zh: 但他热爱教会。

sentences.en: He attended
sentences.zh: 他与母亲和祖母一起参加

sentences.en: Seventh-day
sentences.zh: 基督复临安息日会的

sentences.en: Adventist sermons with his mother and grandmother and would memorise entire chapters of the
sentences.zh: 布道，并能背诵整章的

sentences.en: Bible.
sentences.zh: 《圣经》。

sentences.en: Vernon later dropped out of high school
